subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & SLA targets for MedForward
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rhodes <sam.rhodes@medforward.com>; Priya Singh <priya@medforward.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & SLA targets for MedForward

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Short recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the pain, the goals, and a proposed skeleton for the dedicated (reserved GPU) deployment. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you reiterated
- Inference latency variability at peak that causes downstream timeouts for chart-generation and patient summary flows.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI in an isolated tenancy; cannot co-mingle with other customers.
- Cost predictability: finance needs a capped monthly spend or committed throughput estimate for procurement.

Goals / success criteria we heard
- Stable p95 generation latency <= 120ms for 512-token end-to-end for the summary endpoint.
- Reserved capacity able to sustain baseline throughput of ~600k tokens/day with bursts up to 2M tokens/day for end-of-day processing windows.
- Isolation: private tenant (VPC) with customer-controlled keys; SOC 2 and audit logs required for procurement.

Proposed dedicated capacity configuration (initial recommendation)
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (config F: 4xH100-style dense inference nodes) with private tenancy and tenant-level KV cache.
- Burst policy: allow 3x burst (auto-burst to shared capacity) for predictable peak handling; falls back to smaller quantized variant if bursts are constrained.
- Quantization: 8-bit FP or Q4 for non-critical endpoints to stretch throughput; keep FP16 for the summary endpoint to preserve quality.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime on the dedicated pool with latency SLO of p95 <= 120ms (work with engineering on exact measurement hooks).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Technical kickoff with MedForward infra & security (Connor) — propose Mon Jun 14; shared agenda: VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log export. (Owner: connor_obrien)
- Pricing/commit sketch and draft SOW (Ben) — I will put a first-pass commercial outline and attach the sizing PDF + SLA draft. (ETA: Tue Jun 15)
- Security questionnaires & SOC2 evidence pull (Marissa) — list of artifacts we can provide and timeline for the package. (Owner: marissa_cole)

Attachments in this thread: redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.pdf, redwood_sla-draft_medforward.docx, mop_isolation_sketch.png

Questions for you
1) Confirm the baseline daily token estimate: you mentioned ~500–700k/day — is 600k/day a fair central assumption?
2) Are there any internal procurement deadlines (target PO date) we should be aware of in June/July?

If that all looks right I’ll send the pricing and draft SOW tomorrow and schedule the technical kickoff.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

--
Redwood Inference — High performance LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)
From: Sam Rhodes <sam.rhodes@medforward.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@medforward.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & SLA targets for MedForward

Ben —

Thanks for the crisp recap. This matches our notes; I’ll answer the two questions inline and add a couple of clarifications.

Baseline token estimate
- Yes, 600k/day is a good working number. We currently average ~550k/day but expect a new EHR ingestion cadence to push typical days to ~700k/day during rollout.

Procurement deadlines
- We’d like to have the SOW and commercial terms in place by end of June. Target PO by 15 July to align with our July budget window.

Clarifications / obligations
- Isolation: must be separate tenant with KMS integration and a simple path to on-prem connector later (we may want an air-gapped option in Q4).
- Performance guardrail: if latency SLO is missed for two consecutive production days, we’ll need an auto-failover play to fallback model variant and a credit conversation (we can discuss exact credit terms later).

Please go ahead with the SOW and schedule the kickoff. Connor / Marissa — if you want to add any technical artifacts we should review before Monday, drop them here.

Appreciate it — Sam
Sam Rhodes
Head of ML Platform — MedForward Health
sam.rhodes@medforward.com | +1 617-555-2299

Sam / Priya —

Appreciate the confirmation and the PO timing clarity. Quick follow-up and proposed schedule:

1) SOW & commercial sketch (Ben) — I’ll drop a focused commercial one-pager + SOW outline in HubSpot and GDrive by EOD Mon Jun 14. It will include the pricing bands for 4x and 6x GPU pools, burst policy language, and an initial credit clause tied to SLA misses.

2) Tech kickoff (Connor) — propose Mon Jun 14, 10:00 AM PT. Connor — can you confirm availability? Agenda: VPC peering, KMS flow, monitoring/tracing hooks for latency SLOs, logging/export endpoints.

3) Security artifacts (Marissa) — please attach SOC2 evidence sheet and data-retention policy we can include in the procurement packet. If there are certificate expirations or controlled redactions, flag them here.

4) Procurement ask from MedForward (Sam) — please share the internal legal point-of-contact and the purchase order template or PO terms they prefer. We’ll align the SOW to those constraints.

I’ve uploaded the initial sizing + SLA draft to the Drive link below and attached them to this thread. If everyone is good, I’ll create the HubSpot deal stage update and move to "Commercial Review".

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
